exposure: staff trained within the Neonatal Resuscitation Programme (NRP)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 94,038 infant deaths in Turkey recorded in the Infant Mortality Monitoring System between 2007 and 2012.
finding: Infant mortality rate (IMR) and neonatal mortality rate (NMR) in Turkey significantly declined from 2007 to 2010, plateauing in 2012, with reductions associated with increased rates of hospital birth, caesarean delivery, antenatal care, infant follow-up, and Neonatal Resuscitation Programme (NRP) trained staff.
mod_finding: IMR and NMR significantly decreased with an increased rate of caesarean delivery.
followup_time: 12 months after birth for IMR, neonatal period (typically up to 28 days) for NMR
